name: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
authors: Jinyuan Fang, Yanwen Peng, Xi Zhang, et al. (15 authors); corresponding author Zaiqiao Meng. Lead affiliation: University of Glasgow (with University of Sheffield, University of Cambridge, MBZUAI, NUS, UCL, University of Aberdeen, Leiden University).
venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI / cs.CL / cs.MA). Not yet peer-reviewed as of the survey version; associated framework EvoAgentX appears at EMNLP'25 Demo.
code_url: https://github.com/EvoAgentX/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (companion awesome-list / taxonomy repo). Related open-source framework: https://github.com/EvoAgentX/EvoAgentX
reflection_type: none (survey/analysis). The survey itself does not propose a reflection method; it taxonomizes self-evolution techniques, several of which use verbal-self-critique, learned-critic-model, search-guided, and multi-agent-debate styles of reflection/feedback (e.g., Self-Refine, Reflexion-style verbal feedback, LLM-as-a-judge, evolutionary search).
feedback_source: n/a for the survey as an artifact. Across surveyed methods, the abstracted 'Environment' component supplies feedback via proxy metrics covering self-generated signals, external tools (compiler/interpreter/search), unit tests, environment reward, ground-truth/oracle labels, and LLM-based evaluators.
iteration_structure: n/a (survey). The unified framework abstracts a closed iterative optimisation feedback loop (Execution -> Feedback -> Mutation/Refine) that subsumes single-shot, iterative-refine, tree/MCTS-search, and population/evolutionary structures found in the surveyed literature.
reflection_object: Survey covers the full spectrum of what is reflected on / modified: prompt/context, reasoning chain, action trajectory, memory, tools, reusable skills/workflows, multi-agent topology/architecture, model weights, and the agent's own code/architecture. The framework formalises this as the optimiser's 'search space' (prompt template, tool selection, LLM parameters, architectural).
requires_training: n/a (survey). The taxonomy explicitly spans both training-free in-context/test-time optimisation (prompt optimisation, memory, search) and training-based optimisation (SFT, RL such as PPO/GRPO, DPO/preference) under 'Training-Based Behaviour Optimisation' vs 'Test-Time Behaviour Optimisation'.
reward_or_critic_model: n/a (survey). Surveyed signals include none, self-as-judge (LLM-as-a-judge / Agent-as-a-judge), trained reward/process-reward models (e.g., Math-Shepherd, Skywork-Reward), verifiable rewards, and separate retrospective/meta-optimiser models (e.g., Retroformer policy-gradient retrospective optimisation).
distillation_target: Survey enumerates all reusable-artifact targets: episodic-memory (e.g., A-MEM, Mem0, ReasoningBank), reusable-skill/workflow (e.g., Agent Workflow Memory, AFlow), prompt (prompt optimisation methods), and model-weights (SFT/RL fine-tuning). The framework treats these as alternative loci that the optimiser writes its improvements into.
emergent_vs_engineered: Covers both: RL-emergent reflective behaviour (e.g., R1/Absolute-Zero/R-Zero self-play reasoning lines) and prompt/scaffold-engineered reflection (e.g., Self-Refine, Retroformer, evolutionary prompt optimisation). The survey does not privilege one; it organises them under behaviour optimisation vs. structural/workflow optimisation.
memory_type: n/a (survey). Dedicates a 'Memory Optimization' subsection (1.3) reviewing short-term/scratchpad, long-term-episodic, skill-library, structured-notes/graph (e.g., GraphReader), and playbook/cheatsheet style memories, plus production memory systems (Mem0, A-MEM, Memory-R1, ReasoningBank).
memory_persistence: n/a (survey). Surveyed memory methods span within-episode, cross-episode, cross-task, and cross-session/production persistence; the lifelong-agent framing emphasises cross-task and cross-session adaptation.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (survey). Reviews append-only, self-summarised/curated (compressive memory), retrieval-gated, RL-managed (Memory-R1), and evolution/self-relinking (A-MEM agentic memory; MemEvolve meta-evolution of memory architecture) curation strategies.
error_localization_granularity: n/a (survey). Spans the full granularity range across surveyed methods: holistic/outcome-level, response-level, step-level (process reward models, step-wise preference tuning), block-level (code), and agent-level (multi-agent / topology optimisation).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: n/a (survey). Explicitly distinguishes test-time / intra-task optimisation (refine within a task) from cross-task lifelong evolution (transfer of experience across tasks), the latter being the central motivation ('lifelong agentic systems').
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: n/a (survey). Covers post-hoc-revision (Self-Refine, self-debug), avoidance via cross-episode experience transfer, and mid-trajectory recovery within the broader optimisation loop; not framed as a single mechanism.
task_domains: General agentic tasks plus domain-specific: code/programming, math/reasoning, QA, web-navigation/GUI, tool-use, decision-making, multi-agent collaboration, and specialised domains - biomedicine (medical diagnosis, molecular/drug discovery), finance (financial decision-making), legal reasoning, scientific research, and climate science.
benchmarks: Survey's evaluation section catalogs benchmarks rather than reporting its own: GAIA, AgentBench, SWE-bench, WebArena, BrowseComp, WebWalker, OSWorld, AndroidWorld, Mobile-Bench, API-Bank, ToolQA, MetaTool, MLGym, DataSciBench, MultiAgentBench, plus safety benchmarks (AgentHarm, RedCode, R-Judge, MobileSafetyBench, SafeLawBench).
headline_result: Not a results paper. Headline contribution: a unified conceptual framework abstracting the self-evolving feedback loop into four components (System Inputs I, Agent System A, Environment, Optimiser P), plus the 'Three Laws of Self-Evolving AI Agents' (Endure / Excel / Evolve, inspired by Asimov), used to organise single-agent, multi-agent, and domain-specific optimisation techniques from 2023-2025.
baselines: n/a (survey). It is positioned relative to prior surveys of LLM agents, agent optimisation, prompt optimisation, and multi-agent systems, distinguishing itself by the unified optimiser-centric feedback-loop abstraction and the lifelong/self-evolving lens.
gains_vs_baseline: n/a (survey; no empirical gains reported by the paper itself).
compute_cost_profile: n/a (survey; no compute experiments). Conceptually notes that optimisers vary widely in cost (rule-based heuristics vs. gradient descent vs. Bayesian/MCTS/RL vs. learning-based policy) and discusses efficiency as a design dimension of the search space + optimisation algorithm pair (S, H).
known_limitations: States that self-evolving agentic systems are an emerging direction with open challenges in evaluation (lack of standardised lifelong/self-evolving benchmarks), safety (must maintain stability during modification - the 'Endure' law), alignment/ethics, controllability of autonomous self-modification, and risk of capability regression; calls these critical to effectiveness and reliability.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: n/a (survey). Catalogs the full dependency spectrum across methods (intrinsic-only self-verify, external-tool/verifier, oracle-label/ground-truth, env-reward) via the abstracted Environment/proxy-metric feedback channel; does not itself adjudicate which works without label leakage.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent (survey-level characterisation). The paper does not run controlled experiments but frames efficacy as contingent on the optimiser design, the quality of environmental feedback, and domain constraints; the 'Excel' law explicitly requires that evolution preserve or enhance existing performance, acknowledging regression risk.
calibration_effect: not-measured (survey does not empirically study reasoning-model calibration / 'reasoning tax').
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (survey is not a failure-attribution method; it reviews evaluation and safety considerations but does not provide a failure-mode classifier or step/agent attribution mechanism).
failure_mode_addressed: n/a as a method. As a survey it discusses safety/stability failure modes of self-evolution (capability regression, unsafe self-modification, alignment drift) and reviews safety benchmarks; it does not map to MAST's 14 modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark released by the survey itself. It releases a curated, continuously updated taxonomy/awesome-list repository (EvoAgentX/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents) and is associated with the EvoAgentX open-source evolving-workflow framework.
builds_on: Foundation-model and LLM-agent literature; agent optimisation primitives it synthesises include Self-Refine, Reflexion-style verbal feedback, Retroformer, TextGrad/DSPy, EvoPrompt/Promptbreeder/GEPA (prompt evolution), AFlow/ADAS/GPTSwarm (workflow & multi-agent architecture search), STaR/ToRA (training-based), and R1/Absolute-Zero/R-Zero (RL self-play); Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics (conceptual inspiration for the Three Laws).
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited/extended by follow-up self-evolving and lifelong-agent works including MemEvolve (meta-evolution of agent memory), CoMAS (co-evolving multi-agent systems), FLEX (continuous agent evolution from experience), Alita-G, ReasoningBank, Self-evolving Embodied AI, and domain surveys on agentic AI for wireless/edge networks; ~69 citing works as of mid-2026.
citation_count: 69 (Semantic Scholar, Corpus ID 280566335, retrieved 2026-06-08; 4 highly-influential citations).
reasoning_model_native: Partially. The survey explicitly covers RL-trained reasoning models with built-in/emergent reflection (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-style, Absolute Zero, R-Zero) under 'Reasoning-Based' and RL behaviour optimisation, but is not specific to o1/R1-class models; it treats them as one branch of self-evolution.
on_policy_distillation_link: Relevant. The taxonomy includes distillation- and RL-based self-improvement (e.g., STaR bootstrapping, Chain-of-Agents multi-agent distillation, self-rewarding LMs, self-play RL), which are on-policy distillation / skill-optimisation analogues, but the survey does not single out on-policy distillation as a named category.
